units.text: StreamlineOS / Source architecture review / 24 October 2026
Deepen the seams that carry People facts into payroll, Calendar, charts and AskOS.

Read-only review of representative HRMS and payroll paths. Confirmed defects are distinguished from reasoned risks and proposed target design. The PRD describes desired behavior; it does not certify the code.
Recheck added: Summary · Priority · 24 corners · Executed checks · Existing protections · Source hashes

Fix first: confirmed read-path defect. The HR command-center response requires only hr:analytics:read yet returns payroll gross cost. Its department filter is put in the cache key but omitted from underlying SQL. The frontend hides a card, not the response field. Restrict the response at the backend, make every metric obey the declared filter or reject the unsupported filter, and test raw responses for an analytics-only actor. Problem: Confirmed: Calendar presentation fetches HR directly; the analytics date selector changes attendance while other metrics retain fixed periods.
Solution: Deepen two narrow interfaces: bounded visibility-safe Calendar events and typed metrics with period, unit, coverage and provenance. Keep rendering generic, not metric meaning.
Locality: scope and coverage travel with values. Leverage: charts, export and AskOS. Test surface: dates, partial data, denied source.
Target contracts and schema rules

EmploymentFacts v1 orgId, workerId, engagementId, employmentId, legalEntityId, effective interval, lifecycle and eligibility, sourceVersion. Keep salary/bank out of general reads. Core HR → Workforce, Payroll, insights

TimeInputPackage v1 employmentId, pay period, business calendar/timezone, approved quantities and units, policy version, source watermark, checksum, correction reference, exclusion reason. Workforce → Payroll

PayrollInputSnapshot v1 periodId, generation, schemaVersion, eligible subjects, typed required sections, completeness, source IDs/versions, exact money, checksum, lockedAt/by. Immutable after lock. Payroll Input Period → calculation

InsightMetric v1 metricKey, period, department/entity scope, unit/currency, value, asOf, sourceVersion, coverage and sensitivity class. Unavailable differs from zero. Fact owner → charts, export, AskOS
CalendarEventProjection v1 source type/id/version, start/end/timezone, visibility, safe label, status, deep link, changedAt. No restricted pay detail. Fact owner → Calendar
AskOS read result v1 Actor-scoped safe summary, cited source/version/asOf, redaction and uncertainty. High-impact commands need human approval. HR/Payroll read module → AskOS adapter
These shapes are proposals. Exact Zod fields and wire dates must be reconciled with existing migrations and generated OpenAPI before implementation.
Route and read-model contract plan
Prefer the current URLs. The proposal changes their validated behavior before adding endpoints.

GET /hr/people and employment reads Cursor, limit ≤100 and explicit search/filter. Return worker and effective-employment IDs with source version and permissioned projection; never merge identity and sensitive pay fields. hr:employees:view plus DataScope and object checks; identity/effective-facts namespace.

POST /hr/payroll-inputs/periods/:periodId/build and /lock Accept idempotency and expected period version. Build returns generation, eligibility and validation summary. Lock accepts only the built generation and returns immutable checksum; status conflict is 409. Existing HR payroll-input permissions; compare-and-set transaction; no unverified snapshot cache.

GET /payroll/readiness and POST /payroll/runs/:runId/generate Readiness names missing or corrupt sections and responsible owner. Generate references locked generation/hash and refuses ambiguous or stale input. Payroll-specific permission; versioned run/readiness keys and targeted aggregate invalidation.

GET /hr/analytics-plus Return only non-sensitive metrics for analytics-only actors. Department and period either scope every returned metric or are rejected as unsupported. Payroll cost remains behind its salary-gated route. Actor/scope/permission-specific cache, with every filter included.

GET /hr/calendar Bounded from/to and type filters. Visibility-safe event projections with source/version and changed-at metadata; no raw HR records. HR permission and module gate; source-owner invalidation and Calendar window key.

Every route keeps strict Zod validation, declared response schema, generated OpenAPI parity, 402 module denial, 403 in-tenant denial, 404 cross-tenant miss and 409 version conflict. Backend command transactions own write, audit and outbox intent together.
Interface rules from database to page

DB queries Explicit projections, org + ScopedRead predicate, keyset pagination capped at 100, composite tenant foreign keys, selective indexes including org ID, application-role RLS tests, EXPLAIN buffers.

Route contracts Keep current owner URLs where possible. Strict Zod body/query/params and ResponseSchema; generated OpenAPI vendored to frontend. Add a route only for a missing job; commands carry expected version and idempotency.

Backend cache CacheService versioned namespaces. Key by tenant plus actor/scope/permission version when access shapes data, and all filters/periods. Every writer bumps affected namespaces; test actor isolation and outage behavior.

TanStack Query Entity-local query options co-locate key, query function, contract and staleTime. Keep scoped QueryClient hash. Filter params in key, abort signal forwarded, permission/module gates prevent denied fetches.
Mutation effect Patch exact cached rows when response is sufficient; mark aggregates stale without broad refetch. Test optimistic rollback, paginated lists, revoked access and late approvals.

Pages and visual modules Thin server-gated route; PageState for loading/denied/error/empty/ready. URL owns filter/sort/page. Typed projections feed charts and Calendar. Verify 375/768/1280, light/dark, keyboard and screen reader.

Cross-owner handoff Version, tenant, effective time, source reference, idempotency/correlation, retry and reconciliation. Durable outbox/inbox only where crash-loss matters; do not add hypothetical adapters.

Delivery sequence
0. Contain the analytics exposure. Backend permission and department filters, raw-response tests, cache partitioning.
1. Pin current contracts. Inventory routes, tables, query keys, owners and consumers; add negative-first tests for snapshot corruption and lock races.
2. Deepen Payroll Input Period. Typed versions, eligibility, completeness, generation, compare-and-set lock, old/new calculation comparison and rollback.
3. Recover cross-owner projections. Durable leave-to-payroll intent and idempotent reconciliation; preserve existing Calendar and accounting adapters.
4. Deepen authorized reads. Employment mapping, insight metrics and AskOS access with source provenance and field sensitivity.
5. Simplify frontend orchestration. Action Center adapters, query locality, exact cache effects, typed metric and Calendar presentation; browser role/failure checks.
Contain the insights exposure; then deepen Payroll Input Period.

The first is a confirmed authorization mismatch. The second gives the largest depth and leverage: every payroll run depends on eligibility, provenance, completeness and immutability behind one interface.
Corner-case recheck added to this report

This revision revalidates the first findings, adds five deepening candidates, records 24 corner-case categories and separates confirmed source defects, executed helper behavior, reasoned risks, existing protections and unexecuted release gates.

Confirmed additions: duplicate bank-return rows can fail after partial application; AskOS headcount uses the wrong department identifier type; employee prefetch uses a different key/envelope from the rendered infinite list; payroll document downloads have weaker file-content validation than CSV job downloads.

Important qualification: getAttritionSummary does not inspect its ScopedRead, but hr:analytics:read is currently not a scopable permission. Treat scoped-actor exposure there as a conditional risk, not a demonstrated reachable grant defect. Accountless payees, payout replay checks, full-paid coverage and Calendar leave privacy already exist.
Revised implementation order

0 — immediate correctness Contain payroll cost in analytics response; fix/reject department filter; use canonical department ID in AskOS. Negative-first raw-response and filter tests at the owner interface. No sensitive data in shared cache.

1 — trust the frozen input Typed snapshot generation, explicit eligibility, validation/completeness, CAS lifecycle and exact value handling. Corrupt input rejected; concurrent build/lock proven under PostgreSQL; signed deterministic calculations reconcile.

2 — money and sensitive records Bank-return reconciliation receipts and duplicate handling; restore ScopedRead in five HR violations. Replay/partial-import outcomes explicit; object and field authorization consistent through the interface.

3 — recover downstream facts Durable leave/recruitment follow-up and owner read projections for Calendar, charts and AskOS. Delay, crash, duplicate and reconciliation tests; source version/observed lag visible.

4 — complete client locality Shared prefetch/infinite options, Action Center adapters, precise cache effects, document download validation. Browser evidence for no duplicate initial load, stale decision handling, role denial and valid file delivery.

5 — release evidence Migration/restore rehearsal, accessibility, load/RLS plans and two representative payroll parallel cycles. Named owners sign off supported country/establishment/workforce scope and every unresolved risk.

Problem: Confirmed in source: a return file resolves items from one initial status map. A second PAID row can fail after the first committed; repeated FAILED rows can emit repeated failure events. Whole-file replay coverage does not cover duplicate rows within one file.

Solution: Put parse, preflight, item resolution, duplicate/conflict detection and per-row outcome receipt behind one reconciliation interface. Keep bank formats as real adapters. Return applied, duplicate, rejected, unresolved and conflicting outcomes; do not silently retry money movement.
Depth hides file and state semantics. Locality keeps item resolution with result application. Leverage spans manual CSV and later provider adapters.
Deletion test: Deleting only the parser moves CSV complexity. Deepen parser plus reconciliation behavior; retain format adapters only for actual formats.

Interface tests: Duplicate PAID/FAILED, contradictory rows, itemId/userId disagreement, accountless payee, repeated file, crash after row N and resume. Existing paid-coverage and live-payee uniqueness protections stay.

Problem: Confirmed inconsistent download validation: CSV job paths reject empty/HTML bodies; payroll PDF paths save a successful blob without that check. Reasoned storage risks: upload before DB upsert can orphan a new object; post-update deletion failure can surface an error after replacement succeeded.

Solution: Deepen publication and download interfaces around staged upload, committed document version, cleanup receipt, access-checked delivery, content validation and safe filename. Distinguish published, delivered and paid states; define assisted delivery for accountless workers.
Locality for publication recovery and file validation. Leverage for payslips, tax documents and governed exports.
Deletion test: Removing per-screen download code concentrates real validation and resource cleanup. Keep storage/provider adapters only where actual production and test variants exist.

Interface tests: 200 HTML/empty/truncated PDF, revoked access during job, DB failure after upload, old-object delete retry, expired link, legal hold, accountless recipient. No official filing/issuance claim follows from generating a PDF.
24 corner-case coverage records

This is an evidence and acceptance matrix, not a claim that every row passed. Source inspection, mocked tests, database integration, product browser behavior and provider evidence are different proof levels.

Actor and tenant Analytics-only payroll-cost response remains exposed in source. Scope gate fails five HR sites. Raw HTTP response for analytics-only actor; cross-tenant and child-object access; every salary field in export/search/AI.

Worker identity Accountless payees already supported. Directory/HR/Payroll identifiers remain distinct. Multiple employments, rehire, inactive membership, contractor without userId, same email change; preserve historical result linkage.

Sensitive reach Own-scope tests pass; raw DataScope is an ADR violation. Team helper semantics require catalog reachability review. One ScopedRead decision across view, BGV, forms, templates and download; never default an omitted authority to all.

Snapshot completeness Unknown JSON payloads and numeric fallbacks remain in source. Corrupt/missing required section, missing worker map, no attendance versus zero attendance, eligibility exclusions and hash mismatch must block lock/calculation.

Build / lock / unlock Existing lock rollback tests pass. Expected-status CAS is missing in the HR input-period path. Real competing transactions: build vs lock, two builds, unlock vs generation; generation lease/fencing prevents old worker overwrite.

Money and rates Helper counterexamples executed; ordinary-case tests also pass. Validated exact values, malformed input, non-finite/overflow, negative tie rounding, accumulated rounding and signed rule-pack fixtures.

Time and dates Calendar window and leap-day helper tests pass; product timezone cases not executed. Overnight/DST, half-day, holiday/weekend, timezone changes, leap year, effective date at cutoff, backdated correction after payment.

Payee payout coverage Existing partial-paid and completion tests pass; do not rewrite this protection. Zero eligible payees, held payees, duplicate batch, partial return, failed beneficiary, same payee across live instructions.

Return reconciliation Duplicate within-file PAID/FAILED source path confirmed; not reproduced against DB. Preflight, stable item identity, conflicting duplicates, crash/resume receipt and repeated file. Report partial application explicitly.

Unknown provider outcome Manual CSV and unresolved SENT currently exist; no native provider guarantee. Before adding direct provider: signed callback, replay/order, timeout status enquiry, unknown versus failed, returned payment, safe reconciliation.

Approval freshness Client cache can show 30-second-old approval stage; backend race not demonstrated. Expected run/result revision or server invariant re-check, maker/checker, revocation, edited amount after preview, stale bulk action.

Durable side effects Accounting posting uses inbox/outbox; leave rebuild and accepted-offer follow-ups have logged deferred paths. Crash after source commit, duplicate/out-of-order delivery, retry and dead letter, missed onboarding, explicit reconciliation owner.

Calendar privacy and availability Source hides colleague leave reason; availability records failed coverage instead of free. Source tests inspected. Cancel/update/removal, stale projection, all-day exclusive end, bounded window, hidden source, lost permission, no unauthorized reason.

AskOS contract and provenance Numeric department ID conflicts with canonical text/UUID-shaped contract. Scoped attrition risk is conditional because analytics key is not scopable. Canonical ID, no raw owner-table rule duplication, effective policy applicability, source-specific citations, latest-ten truncation, denial before model call.

Backend cache Key-shape gate passes; this does not prove all filters or every invalidation. Writer-to-read matrix, permission version, namespace failure, stale fill racing mutation, actor discriminator, broad versus narrow metric scope.

Browser cache and revocation Org/user scoped client, logout/switch clear and cross-tab refresh paths exist; focused isolation tests pass. Remote revoke while page open, no storage event, stale access cache, mutation server denial, secret view removal and late HTTP response.

SSR and hydration Employee single-query prefetch cannot hydrate client infinite-query key. Same options/key/envelope/filter on both callers; count initial requests and verify Next navigation abort/permission gate.

Lists and DB performance Bounded-contract gate passes. Bounds alone do not prove completeness or index quality. Stable keyset tie-break, consistent counts/hasMore, limit+1, avoid silent 100-row truncation, RLS application-role EXPLAIN buffers, query-count budgets.

Schema and wire contracts Local OpenAPI vendor matches. Parity gate compares origin/main and finds eight new chat fields outside HR; frozen baseline has HR findings. Pin document revision and reconcile HR-specific baseline entries; unknown enums/nulls, money/date wire types, partial response and 204.

Exports and file delivery CSV jobs have content guards; some PDF callers do not. Async export reauthorization exists in named paths. Job ownership/scope re-check at execution and download, empty/HTML files, CSV formula escaping, expiring URLs, assisted accountless delivery.

Storage and retention Form16 replacement ordering and retention coverage need review; no legal compliance conclusion. Orphan cleanup, failed deletion after commit, legal hold, retention version, subject export, audit redaction, backup/restore references.

UI and accessibility Skills Matrix axe and smaller Payroll visual tests exist; no full close-month mobile/browser proof. Loading/denied/error/empty/partial, keyboard and screen reader, 375/768/1280 light/dark, stale success, slow/aborted network and reopened requests.

Migration and rollback Composite tenant FKs already present; no evidence of absent RLS from source alone. Expand/backfill/compare/enforce/retire, one write owner, resumable backfill, source mapping quarantine, old version read, immutable payroll history.

Operations and support Static gate and focused-test evidence only; live operations not exercised. Trace correlation, projection lag, cache invalidation failures, import row outcomes, outbox backlog, restore drill, source checksum and two parallel payroll cycles.
Checks executed during the second pass

Backend focused Jest PASS — 7 suites, 67 tests Sensitive-reach, input lock rollback, locked-input pull/replay, bank-return partial/replay, full-paid completion and ordinary money tests. These mocks do not prove competing DB transactions or the newly found duplicate-file case.
Frontend focused Jest PASS — 3 suites, 31 tests Query scope isolation, HR Calendar window and analytics honesty. These do not prove source permission enforcement or full product browser behavior.

Backend scope gate FAIL — 5 HR DataScope violations hr-sensitive.service:125; sensitive-reach:4,10; background-verification.service:17; hr-forms-submissions.service:204. Gate self-test passed. ADR-0005 is the accepted design.

Frontend query-scope gate FAIL — 12 inline key sites Calendar/booking/workflows/meeting-workspace and ai-confirm-action plus other paths. Gate self-test passed. This is a key-factory rule violation, not evidence of tenant leakage.
Backend cache key-shape gate PASS 6,129 files scanned by the gate; it verifies resolver reachability and shape relationships, not metric authorization/filter completeness. Self-test passed.

Backend bounded-contract gate PASS — 0 in-scope violations Checks request bounds in declared contract. It cannot prove internal query completeness, source eligibility or query plans. Self-test passed.
OpenAPI vendor freshness PASS Local frontend artifact matches local backend artifact; freshness against a deployed release is separate. Self-test passed.
Request drift gate PASS — Timesheets only 73 calls; 73 resolved. This script's current scope is Timesheets. It provides no HRMS-wide request-drift certification. Self-test passed.

Response parity gate FAIL — 8 new chat required fields against origin/main 1bd1827cb Outside HR scope and concurrent work; do not label these HR defects. Global baseline debt and uncomparable calls remain; align the release document revision before sign-off. Self-test passed.
Exact money helper probe Counterexamples executed 1.005 → 100 paise; 100.005 → 10001; 12abc → 1200; Infinity non-finite. Helper behavior proven, production input reachability unproven.

Initial Jest runs could not write transforms under the sandbox TEMP path. Both suites were rerun successfully with workspace-local temporary caches, which were removed afterwards. No application code or repository tests were edited.
Retain these existing deep seams

Payroll payout: live-payee partial unique index, batch creation replay, full paid-coverage completion, and run-lock/reversal CAS. Sources: db/schema/payroll/payout.ts:66-77; payout/lib/payout-run-completion.ts:108-155; payout/locking.service.ts:138-160,311-435.

Calendar: registered HR source adapters and visibility-safe leave projections. Colleague leave reason is omitted; availability read failure is failed coverage, not free time. Sources: hr/hr-calendar-source.ts:129-134; calendar/calendar-availability.service.ts:153-166,251-258.
Accounting: Payroll uses PostingCommandService and an idempotent payout-posting consumer. Do not replace this with direct journal writes.

Client identity scope: QueryProvider creates org/user-scoped clients and clears on logout/switch. Access invalidation also has cross-tab handling; remote revocation still requires backend enforcement.

Honest capabilities: statutory filing paths describe export-only behavior; bank returns are manual CSV. Generated files are not proof of authority submission, payment, settlement or official issuance.
Design discipline and migration safeguards

Depth: fewer facts a caller must know, with more business correctness behind the interface. File count and line ratios do not measure it. Locality: change, failure and verification concentrate with the fact owner. Leverage: one interface serves Payroll, Calendar, charts or AskOS without duplicating policy.

Seam and adapter: use an in-process interface for deterministic values and normalization. The current query-chain mocks are not a PostgreSQL stand-in. Database races require an isolated PostgreSQL fixture under the application role; do not introduce a generic repository module just to mock Drizzle.
